note: Single source of truth for /knowledge/audit-readiness-checklist and for public/audit-readiness-checklist.xlsx. The page imports this file; scripts/build-audit-checklist.py reads the same file to build the workbook. Edit here, then re-run the script so the two cannot drift.

groups.title: The close and the trial balance
groups.blurb: Nothing else on this list survives a trial balance that is still moving. Fix the base first.
items: Final trial balance agreed to the general ledger, with a stated cut-off and no entries posted after it outside a documented log.
Opening balances agreed to the prior year signed financial statements, line by line, including any prior period adjustment.
Every bank account reconciled to statement, with reconciling items aged, explained, and cleared where they should be.
Suspense, clearing and holding accounts cleared to nil, or the residual explained and supported.
Intercompany balances agreed both ways and eliminated, with differences resolved rather than parked.
Cut-off tested either side of the reporting date for revenue, purchases, and accruals, with the sample retained.
Manual journal listing for the period, with the largest entries and anything posted outside normal hours ready to explain without being asked.

groups.title: Supporting schedules
groups.blurb: One schedule per balance that carries judgment, each agreeing to the ledger and each showing its own workings.
items: Fixed asset register agreed to the ledger, with additions, disposals, and the depreciation charge reconciled to the movement.
Lease schedule recomputed under IFRS 16, with the incremental borrowing rate documented and the reasoning for it retained.
Inventory count sheets, the valuation basis, and the obsolescence provision with the data behind it.
Receivables ageing tied to the ledger, with the expected credit loss model, its inputs, and the evidence for the loss rates applied.
Payables listing and accruals schedule, with the basis for each accrual rather than a prior year figure rolled forward.
Provisions schedule showing opening, movement and closing, with the evidence supporting each estimate.
Borrowings schedule with maturity analysis, covenants, and the covenant position measured at the reporting date.
Equity movement covering share issues, dividends declared and paid, and every reserve.

groups.title: Judgments and estimates
groups.blurb: This is where audits slow down. Not because the number is wrong, but because the reasoning was never written down.
items: A short memo for each significant judgment, stating the conclusion, the alternatives considered, and why they were set aside.
Going concern assessment covering at least twelve months from the expected date of approval, with the cash flow forecast and its assumptions attached.
Impairment indicators considered and documented, including where the conclusion was that no impairment was needed.
Revenue recognition policy tested against the actual contracts in the period, not against the policy as written last year.
Related party listing confirmed with those charged with governance, covering transactions, balances, and terms.
Contingent liabilities and legal matters listed, with the position confirmed in writing by counsel.

groups.title: Controls and process evidence
groups.blurb: The auditor is testing whether the control operated, not whether it exists on paper. Evidence of review is the part most often missing.
items: Delegation of authority current, approved, and matching the approvals that actually happened during the period.
Bank mandates and payment approval limits reconciled to what the bank has on file.
Segregation of duties over payments, payroll and journal posting, with the conflicts that remain identified and compensated.
System access rights reviewed for leavers, joiners and role changes, with the review evidenced and dated.
Reconciliations showing evidence of review as well as preparation, by someone other than the preparer.
Change log for the accounting system covering the period, including configuration changes and who approved them.

groups.title: The request list
groups.blurb: The PBC list is the single biggest driver of how long fieldwork runs. Answering it in advance is the cheapest thing on this page.
items: Request the PBC list before the fieldwork date rather than receiving it on the first morning.
One named owner and one date against every item, agreed with the owner rather than assigned to them.
Recurring items from last year answered and filed before the auditor asks for them again.
Evidence in a single indexed folder, named so an item can be found by its reference without a phone call.
An open items register with owner and status, updated daily during fieldwork and shared with the audit team.

groups.title: Group and reporting
groups.blurb: Where there is a group, the consolidation is usually the last thing ready and the first thing questioned.
items: Consolidation working showing eliminations, non-controlling interests, and the translation of foreign components.
Uniform accounting policies confirmed across components, with any departures identified and adjusted.
Disclosure checklist run against the standards actually in issue for the reporting period.
Draft financial statements circulated to those charged with governance before fieldwork closes, not after.
